questions.q: What does the summary say the Celts' wealth was built on?
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the Celts grew rich by trading salt and salt-cured goods such as ham.

questions.q: Why did the Celts prefer bronze tools in their salt mines?
questions.why: Lesson 1 credits the Celts with noticing that bronze, unlike iron, does not rust.

questions.q: How did Britain help push the colonies into the Revolutionary War?
a: By restricting the salt trade and taxing it heavily
By closing American ports to tea
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Britain kept cheap salt from reaching local producers and raised taxes until conflict exploded in 1775.

questions.q: What environmental damage did brine extraction cause in Cheshire?
a: Sinkholes, vanished pastures, and broken rail lines
Polluted rivers that killed all the fish
Forest fires that burned for years
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes huge sinkholes swallowing parts of towns and wrecking roads, bridges and pipes.

questions.q: Who benefited from the tax Cheshire introduced in 1891?
a: Big companies that could afford it
The workers who mined the salt
The towns that owned the springs
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the flat tax crippled small producers and let large firms take over the industry.
